rv.q: Craig, a fine actor in the past, is a victim of all the directing detritus.
Watching the production and often being very engaged, I kept thinking how much better this 'Macbeth' would be if staged in-the-round at NYTW or on a thrust stage at the Public Theater.
This 'Macbeth' struck me as a bit bloodless.

When you consider what might have been—a Macbeth with awe-inspiring sets and transportive costumes, the full complement of Broadway tricks that make ordinary productions extraordinary—particularly with top notch talent like Craig and Negga leading the way, you can only think of the missed opportunity.

cn.t: Critics find this Macbeth a missed opportunity, with detached performances from Craig and company failing to ignite Shakespeare's drama. The production's intimate staging feels lost on Broadway, while directorial flourishes prioritize gore over emotional impact.
